about: Who must agree before clemency is granted, in each state, D.C., the territories and the federal government, as of 2026. Read by src/simulation/justice/clemency-rules.ts. Each row's gates are tried in order and the first whose offense condition matches applies. mustAgree lists every body whose yes a grant needs, in the order a petition reaches them; 'executive' is the governor (or the President). advisory is a body the grantor hears from without a veto: referral 'required' means the law makes the grantor refer the case or wait for a report (reportWithinDays caps the wait where the law does), and 'optional' means the grantor may ask. referralBasis 'read' means the rule was read; 'estimated-from-common-rule' means it starts from the most common read rule, as the row's note says, until research reads it. toRead lists what research can still read; nothing in it is shown to a player. unansweredRecommendationTakesEffect records a law under which a board's recommendation takes effect when the grantor does not act. A board's members are 'appointed' or a list of the offices that sit on it ex officio. basis: P = constitution or statute text read, G = a state guide that quotes the clause, O = an official page. From Research 4's table, Drive 1W7xojSc3HmxZ5QPGBVEkiZiPXI4_xtqzGHbd82r-kkg (9:20 p.m. 9/28) with its 10:07 p.m. corrections, and the CTO's 9:54 p.m. ruling (record the real gate, not a bucket), 10:24 p.m. ruling (Arizona, North Dakota) and 10:32 p.m. addendum (no value shows UNKNOWN).

gates.note: A.R.S. sec. 31-402(A): for a felony committed before January 1, 1994 the governor may not act unless the board first recommends.

For a later felony the board may recommend and the governor may act alone. A unanimous commutation recommendation the governor does not act on within 90 days 'automatically becomes effective' (A.R.S. 31-402(C), (D)).

notes: The board's recommendation does not bind the governor.
